name: Question 4
worked_solution:
By the scalar function multiple rule, we have

$$
(u(t)g(t))^{′}=u(t){g}^{′}(t)+{u}^{′}(t)g(t).
$$

Let's find ${u}^{′}(t)$ and ${g}^{′}(t).$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{e}^{-t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2{e}^{-t},\,\frac{4}{t},\,0⟩ \\ {u}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}) \\  & =t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)g(t))^{′} & =u(t){g}^{′}(t)+{u}^{′}(t)g(t) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}⟨-2{e}^{-t},\,\frac{4}{t},\,0⟩+t⟨2{e}^{-t},\,4\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-{t}^{2}{e}^{-t},\,2t,\,0⟩+⟨2t{e}^{-t},\,4t\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,2t⟩ \\  & =⟨2t{e}^{-t}-{t}^{2}{e}^{-t},\,2t+4t\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,2t⟩ \\  & =⟨t{e}^{-t}(2-t),\,2t(1+2\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,2t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Find (u(t)g(t))′ where g(t)=⟨2e−t,4ln⁡t,2⟩ and u(t)=12t2.

a
⟨te−t(2−t),2t(1+2ln⁡t),2t⟩
b
 ⟨t2e−t,t2(1+2ln⁡t),1⟩
c
 ⟨2−t,2(1+2ln⁡t),t⟩
d
 ⟨e−t,2ln⁡t,2t−1⟩
e
⟨te−t,1+2ln⁡t,2t⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

By the scalar function multiple rule, we have (u(t)g(t))′=u(t)g′(t)+u′(t)g(t).

Let's find u′(t) and g′(t). g′(t)=⟨ddt(2e−t),ddt(4ln⁡t),ddt(2)⟩=⟨−2e−t,4t,0⟩u′(t)=ddt(12t2)=t

Therefore, we obtain (u(t)g(t))′=u(t)g′(t)+u′(t)g(t)=12t2⟨−2e−t,4t,0⟩+t⟨2e−t,4ln⁡t,2⟩=⟨−t2e−t,2t,0⟩+⟨2te−t,4tln⁡t,2t⟩=⟨2te−t−t2e−t,2t+4tln⁡t,2t⟩=⟨te−t(2−t),2t(1+2ln⁡t),2t⟩.
